evidence: Design requires actual partial progress before deliberately held native completion, distinct from parser/provider/browser doubles.
Each explicit response remains one bounded Foundation task/reservation; uncertainty blocks new work and reconnect is read-only.
Artifact/proposal extraction is restricted to proven successful non-revoked output; exact existing Foundation plan scope/hash/revision/expiry is server-derived.
Owner approval uses real Foundation authority and explicitly adds neither broad tools nor automatic enqueue; fresh-owner rejection/approval is immutable and idempotent.
SSE admission/lifetime/backpressure/session revocation and cursor reset/reopen are explicit acceptance gates.
contractFreezeChecks: Publish concrete finite event/retention/context/artifact/proposal limits and exact DTO shapes before test authoring.
Define cursor gap/ahead/foreign behavior and decision expiry boundary precisely in the implementation contract.
Approval decision replay must not renew expiry or create a second Foundation decision; failure between Foundation approval and proposal journal update needs atomicity or safe idempotent recovery.
Final authoritative output versus already-persisted partial text must be represented distinctly after cancellation or provider-tool refusal.
reviewScope: Independent design review only; no production implementation examined and no runtime qualification claimed. Contract freeze checks are implementation obligations already implied by acceptance criteria, not new scope.
